blocks.prompt: 12. How many numbers of three digits are divisible by 7?
blocks.explanation:
Yeh ginti (counting) ka sawal hai. 7 ke teen hindson wale multiples (105, 112, 119, ...) har dafa 7 barhte hain, yani yeh A.P. hai jis ka \(d = 7\).
Find kya karna hai? Is A.P. ki kitni terms hain.
Plan: pehla aur aakhri teen hindson wala multiple dhoondna, phir \(a_n = l\) se \(n\) nikalna.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: teen hindson wale numbers 100 se 999 tak hain.
Humein find karna hai: in mein se kitne 7 se poori tarah divide hote hain.
Tareeqa: 7 ke multiples 7, 7 se barhte hain, is liye A.P. banate hain. Aakhri term \(l = a_1 + (n - 1)d\) se terms ki ginti \(n\) mil jati hai. Is tarah humein ek ek gin'na nahi parta.

Pehla multiple dhoondein
\[100 = 7 \times 14 + 2\]
\[a_1 = 7 \times 15 = 105\]
Kyun: 100 ko 7 se divide kiya: 14 aur baqi 2. \(7 \times 14 = 98\) sirf do hindson ka hai, is liye agla multiple \(7 \times 15 = 105\) pehla teen hindson wala hai.

Aakhri multiple dhoondein
\[999 = 7 \times 142 + 5\]
\[l = 7 \times 142 = 994\]
Kyun: 999 ko 7 se divide kiya: 142 aur baqi 5. \(7 \times 143 = 1001\) chaar hindson ka ho jata hai, is liye aakhri teen hindson wala multiple 994 hai.

\(n\) nikalein
\[994 = 105 + (n - 1)7\]
\[889 = (n - 1)7\]
\[n - 1 = 127\]
\[n = 128\]
Kyun: 994 is A.P. \(105, 112, \ldots, 994\) ki aakhri yani \(n\)th term hai. Dono taraf se 105 minus kiya, phir 7 se divide, phir 1 jama.
Dhyan dein: Sirf \((994 - 105) \div 7 = 127\) likh kar ruk jana aam ghalti hai; pehli term bhi ginni hoti hai, is liye 1 jama karna zaroori hai.

Tasdeeq: doosre tareeqe se
\[142 - 15 + 1 = 128 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Multiples \(7 \times 15\) se \(7 \times 142\) tak hain. 15 se 142 tak ke numbers gin'en to \(142 - 15 + 1 = 128\) aate hain. Dono tareeqon se ek hi jawab.
blocks.final_answer: \(128\) teen hindson wale numbers 7 se divide hote hain.
